notes: Customer: omnichannel contact center platform used by retail and telco customers.
Primary pain: unpredictable token costs and latency during large incident bursts (outages) and seasonal peaks (Black Friday, holiday returns).
Key quote: 'We need guaranteed behavior during 10x traffic events — can't have agents waiting on long tail LLM calls.' — VP Product
Target workloads: real-time agent assist (context window ~6k tokens), ticket summarization (batch nightly), automated tool-calling for account lookups.
Acceptable latency: interactive agent assist target p95 < 500ms under normal load; p95 < 900ms under 10x spikes with graceful degradation.
Throughput target: support 3k concurrent agent sessions baseline, scale to 30k during peak.
Model preferences: open-model families (gpt-style open weights) with quantized variants; interested in model routing by cost/latency tiers.
Routing/fallback needs: deterministic fallback to smaller/local model when Dedicated capacity saturated; preferring prefix/KV cache for repeated dialogs.
Data residency: US-only for retail customers; some EU tenants require EU region isolation.
Cost sensitivity: high — customer runs large nightly summarization and measures per-ticket cost; wants Optimize recommendations and quantization guidance.
Observability ask: token-level cost attribution per agent, end-to-end tracing from agent UI to model token emission, and alerts on regen/rollback rates.
POC notes: storage for 7-day request logs ballooned; exploring sample-based logging to satisfy audit while controlling cost.
Compliance: SOC2 readiness required; customer will run Redwood through third-party security assessment if POC metrics are satisfactory.
